- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak heights.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — dampen subsequent forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model overestimates recovery — adjust downward bias in later forecast days.
- Model underestimates downward moves when sentiment is negative and recent price is stable — add 2–3% downward bias to early forecast days.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model tends to overfit recent volatility — smooth forecast curve with exponential decay filter.
- Forecast horizon 30d often overestimates mean reversion — reduce final 5–7 days by 3–5% if sentiment is weak or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small reversals, model fails to capture mean reversion — apply slight downward bias to middle forecast days.
- Model often ignores sentiment when price is near support/resistance — if sentiment is negative and price near recent low, add 1–2% downward adjustment.
